subject: Wexler Systems - eastus2 regional outage: request to divert traffic + circuit diversion
messages:
From: Rachel Lopez <rachel.lopez@wexler-systems.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: adam.klein@wexler-systems.com
Date: Tue, 30 Apr 2029 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: [URGENT] eastus2 - sustained latency + 502s impacting checkout

Dylan —

We're seeing a sustained latency increase across eastus2 that started ~07:45 PT and has grown into 30-40% 502 error rates on our write-heavy checkout path. Our telemetry shows token throughput dropped and a lot of retries from our side. This started right after a regional maintenance window ended (we think).

Key metrics (last 30m):
- p95 latency: 1.8s (baseline 220ms)
- 502 ratio: 0.34
- token/sec: -42% vs rolling avg

This is customer-impacting — several orders failing and queued. We need an immediate plan: can you divert our traffic away from eastus2 to a healthy region (canary first) and engage any circuit-level mitigation you have?

Attaching a screenshot of our dashboard and a short export of the failing requests. Please treat as P0.

Thanks,
Rachel Lopez
Senior SRE, Wexler Systems
[rachel.lopez@wexler-systems.com]

[Attachment: wexler_latency_snapshot_20290430.png (image/png)]
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: Rachel Lopez <rachel.lopez@wexler-systems.com>, Adam Klein <adam.klein@wexler-systems.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Apr 2029 08:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] eastus2 - sustained latency + 502s impacting checkout

Rachel — thanks for the quick signal and the captures. I'm escalating internally and proposing two immediate actions:

1) Activate a temporary circuit diversion (circuit-breaker) on eastus2 for Wexler traffic to throttle error amplification and give us breathing room. This will short-circuit heavy write flows and return a 503 with Retry-After for a short window while we triage.

2) Canary reroute: divert 10% of traffic to us-west2, evaluate error/lats for 5 min, then expand to 60% if healthy.

Soojin — can you confirm we have capacity headroom in us-west2 to absorb the canary and the steps to apply a fast-routing policy? Marissa — FYI on potential fallback model variant if we need lower memory quantization for throughput.

I'll loop back with the exec ask once we have confirmation of the capacity and the expected customer-visible impact (credits, SLA).

Dylan Brooks
Senior Escalations Manager, Redwood Inference
[dylan_brooks@redwood.com]

Quick ops update — we can perform both items. Readout below and actions I will execute within the next 10 minutes pending your go:

Operational plan (safe short-circuit + canary):
- Step 1 (T+0m): Apply tenant-scoped circuit-breaker on Wexler's write route in eastus2 (return 503 + Retry-After: 10s). Purpose: stop retry storms and relieve contention on KV cache. Duration: 5-10m, extendable.
- Step 2 (T+2m): Add routing policy to divert 10% of Wexler traffic to us-west2 via weighted routing (policy id: route-wexler-0429). Monitor errors and queue depth for 5 minutes.
- Step 3 (T+8m): If canary metrics: p95 < 400ms and 502 ratio < 1%, expand to 60% over 4 minutes.

Capacity check: us-west2 currently has ~28% headroom on the serving pools for medium token-length workloads. We'll reserve an extra pool slice (2x machines) and enable aggressive KV cache warmup for the canary traffic.

Attachments: runbook-circuit-diversion-v2.pdf (ops steps, rollback instructions).

Risks: if cache warming fails or model mismatch occurs, we may see transient elevated latencies — we'll hold expansion until we confirm canary stability.

If you want me to proceed, say "go" and I'll execute.

— Soojin
Principal Incident Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — a few product/finance flags to note before broad traffic diversion:

- Cross-region diversion will change per-token cost for Wexler (egress + different hardware price). We should surface a short note to Wexler that traffic will be rerouted and we will do a post-incident usage reconciliation.
- If we expand beyond canary we should also consider pinning Wexler to a lower-memory model variant (reduced KV footprint) as a fallback to preserve throughput. This may slightly change generation quality on edge cases; call this out in the comms.
- Executive steering: because this is >30% 502s and revenue-impacting, I recommend we ask for an exec-level exception to authorize immediate diversion and a one-off credit (if required) so CS has authorization to make customers whole.

Dylan — please raise for Sean's approval (copying him). Also putting a 30-minute bridge on hold after canary expansion so we can decide next steps.

Marissa Cole
Director, Platform Reliability

Dylan — execute the Ops plan from Soojin. Approve circuit-breaker and canary diversion up to 60% as long as Soojin certifies the canary health checks. Approve the one-off customer credit if Finance signs off after post-incident review.

Please publish a short customer-facing note to Wexler (cc: Adam) saying: 1) we diverted traffic to reduce failed requests, 2) we will reconcile usage and propose credits if material, 3) we'll follow up with a detailed timeline and root-cause hypotheses within 48 hours. Keep language crisp and non-technical.

I'll join the bridge if the canary fails or once we hit 60% expansion.
